claim.pdf_says:
INTERFACE-ID.  interface-name-1  [ AS literal-1 ]
    [ INHERITS FROM { interface-name-2 }  ... ]
    [ USING { parameter-name-1 }  ... ] .

(printed underlining, verified on the rendered page at 300 dpi: INTERFACE-ID, AS, INHERITS and USING each carry an underline; FROM carries NO underline)
claim.markdown_says:
```
INTERFACE-ID.  interface-name-1  [ AS literal-1 ]
    [ INHERITS FROM { interface-name-2 }  … ]
    [ USING { parameter-name-1 }  … ] .
```

(no <u> markup, and no '> **Figure notes (...)**' paragraph follows the fence)
claim.why_it_matters: Per 5.2.1/5.2.2 (lines 2628 and 2641 of the transcription's own text) underlined uppercase words are KEYWORDS — required — while non-underlined uppercase words are OPTIONAL words that may be omitted. In the printed 11.6.2 format FROM is not underlined, so 'INHERITS interface-name-2' with FROM omitted is legal COBOL. The fenced transcription records no underlining at all and carries no Figure notes paragraph, so a reader/implementer treats FROM as required — the exact falsely-restrictive-syntax loss this sweep is hunting. The transcription already has an established mechanism for this: 218 other figures carry a '> **Figure notes (...)**' blockquote naming the underlined words (e.g. 11.7.2 METHOD-ID at line 13034, 12.3.6.2 OBJECT-COMPUTER at line 13746). Section 11.6.2 is missing its instance.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED by independent pixel measurement of the 300 dpi render of PDF page 298 (printed folio 268), plus corroboration from the standard's own text and examples. I tried to refute this on four fronts and failed on all four. (1) DOES THE PRINTED PAGE REALLY UNDERLINE THE WAY THE CLAIM SAYS? Yes. I cropped the 11.6.2 general-format block and scanned for horizontal ink runs beneath each word. Measured word bounding boxes and underline runs (image x-coordinates, 2550x3300 render): line 1 (y~955-1000), underline row y=990: INTERFACE-ID box x=295-586, underline run x=297-572 (underline stops before the period); AS box x=989-1035, underline run x=994-1034. Both underlined. line 2 (y~1015-1058), underline row y=1062: INHERITS box x=382-567, underline run x=384-566. FROM box x=586-697 — NO underline run anywhere in the band. The only long run on that row is the INHERITS one. line 3 (y~1075-1120), underline row y=1134: USING box x=381-499, underline run x=384-497. Underlined. I then re-ran the FROM band (x=586-700, y=1056-1078) at progressively looser thresholds to rule out a faint or anti-aliased rule: dark-pixel count under FROM = 0 at threshold 128, 0 at 180, 0 at 220, and still 0 at 245 (essentially 'any non-white ink at all'), while the same band under INHERITS yields 183 / 548 / 549 / 549. There is categorically no underline under FROM. The claim's reading of the glyphs is exactly right. (2) IS THE 'MISSING' MARKUP ACTUALLY PRESENT SOMEWHERE NEARBY (reflowed, adjacent line, different notation)? No. In the master transcription specs/ISO_COBOL.md the 11.6.2 fence is lines 12972-12977; line 12978 is blank and line 12979 is ''. There is no Figure notes blockquote, no markup, and no adjacent prose recording the underlining. The extracted page-298.md slice agrees (fence at lines 17-21, next content is the 11.6.3 anchor at line 23). Both quotations in the claim are accurate transcriptions of their sources. (3) IS IT MERE FORMATTING WITH NO MEANING CHANGE? No — this one genuinely changes which source text is legal. 5.2.2 Keywords (line 2626-2628): 'They are shown in uppercase and underlined in general formats. They are required in order to select the functionality associated with that keyword.' 5.2.3 Optional words (line 2639-2641): 'They are shown in uppercase and not underlined in general formats. They may be written to add clarity when the clause or phrase in which they are defined is written in the source unit.' So a non-underlined FROM is an optional word that MAY BE OMITTED. (4) STRONGEST INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION — THE STANDARD CONTRADICTS THE FLATTENED FIGURE IN ITS OWN EXAMPLES. The Annex example programs repeatedly write INHERITS with FROM omitted: 'CLASS-ID. CheckingAccount INHERITS Base.' (line 45770), 'CLASS-ID. Account INHERITS Base.' (46001), 'CLASS-ID. CheckingAccount INHERITS Account.' (46047), 'CLASS-ID. AccountCollection INHERITS Base USING X.' (46420), 'CLASS-ID. Employee INHERITS Base.' (46487), 'CLASS-ID. Account INHERITS Base.' (46609). A compiler built from the flattened fence would reject every one of these ISO-authored examples. That settles it beyond any argument from the glyphs alone. (5) THE CONVENTION IS REAL AND 11.6.2 IS A GAP IN IT. The transcription carries 225 '**Figure notes' blockquotes, 180 of which use the exact phrase 'are underlined in the printed standard'. The two cited exemplars check out: 11.7.2 METHOD-ID notes at line 13034 and 12.3.6.2 OBJECT-COMPUTER notes at line 13747, both naming underlined vs non-underlined words. 11.6.2 has no instance. Minor inaccuracies in the claim, none of which affect the verdict: the section citations should be 5.2.2 (keywords, required, underlined) and 5.2.3 (optional words, not underlined) — the claim wrote '5.2.1/5.2.2', and 5.2.1 is the meta-language element list, not the optional-word rule; the Figure-notes count is 225 occurrences (215 at line start), not 218; and the OBJECT-COMPUTER notes are at line 13747, not 13746.
verdict.corrected_description:
REAL, normative. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 12972-12977 (§11.6.2 INTERFACE-ID paragraph, General format; PDF page 298 / printed folio 268) transcribes the general format into a plain code fence that records no underlining and carries no '> **Figure notes (...)**' blockquote, so every uppercase word in the figure reads as equally required. On the printed page, verified by pixel measurement of a 300 dpi render, INTERFACE-ID, AS, INHERITS and USING are underlined but FROM is NOT (zero ink in the underline band beneath FROM even at a near-white threshold of 245, against 549 pixels beneath INHERITS). Per 5.2.2, underlined uppercase words are keywords and are required; per 5.2.3, non-underlined uppercase words are optional words that may be omitted. The flattened fence therefore loses the fact that 'INHERITS interface-name-2' without FROM is legal COBOL — a falsely-restrictive-syntax loss. The standard's own Annex examples confirm the omission is legal, writing e.g. 'CLASS-ID. CheckingAccount INHERITS Base.' (line 45770) and 'CLASS-ID.  AccountCollection INHERITS Base USING X.' (line 46420).

FIX: add the established Figure notes blockquote after the line-12977 fence, e.g. '> **Figure notes (INTERFACE-ID paragraph general format).** `INTERFACE-ID`, `AS`, `INHERITS`, and `USING` are underlined in the printed standard (required words). `FROM` is **not** underlined — it is an optional word and may be omitted, so `INHERITS interface-name-2` is legal. The terminating period follows the closing bracket of the USING phrase.'

SWEEP — THIS IS A PATTERN, NOT A ONE-OFF. The same INHERITS-FROM underline loss appears in at least three sibling figures that also lack Figure notes and must be fixed in the same change set:
  * line 12817 — §11.3.2 CLASS-ID paragraph general format ('[ INHERITS FROM { object-class-name-2 } … ]'), fenced, no Figure notes; the fence also flattens the non-underlined `IS` in '[ IS  FINAL ]'.
  * line 12585 — the interface-definition skeleton ('where interface-definition is:'), fenced, no Figure notes.
  * line 12539 — the class-definition skeleton, which is not even fenced (plain text using ideographic-space indentation), no Figure notes.
Recommend a targeted re-check of every general format containing INHERITS, and more broadly an audit for figures whose fence contains an uppercase word that is an optional word in print.
